input: In a series of batch tests carried out at 298 K, the adsorption of a dye from water onto a metal-organic framework was investigated in some detail. The fitted Langmuir capacity came out at 125 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 5, which gives a sense of the uptake that the material can ultimately accommodate under the conditions studied. When the adsorbent was dosed at 0.9 g L-1, the removal after 120 min reached 81% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1, a result that speaks to the practical effectiveness of the material over the timescale of the test. Batch tests hold the liquid and the adsorbent together in a closed vessel, so the measured removal reflects the change in the liquid concentration over the contact time. It should nevertheless be kept in mind that the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 5 only, and that capacity at other pH values was not measured, so the figures that have been obtained should be understood as belonging specifically to the conditions under which the tests were performed rather than as properties that can be carried over without qualification to different conditions.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework removed 81% of the initial dye concentration after 120 min in batch tests at 298 K. The initial dye concentration was 50 mg L-1 and the adsorbent dose was 0.9 g L-1. Batch tests hold the liquid and adsorbent together in a closed vessel, so the measured removal is the change in the liquid concentration over the contact time. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 125 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 5. Removal is stated against the initial concentration, so the percentage and the starting value together fix what the tests achieved. The Langmuir capacity is a fitted quantity: it is the plateau of the fitted isotherm, obtained from the batch data, and it is reported for pH 5 only. Capacity at other pH values was not measured. The result therefore describes uptake under the tested conditions — the stated temperature, dose, contact time, and starting concentration — and the closing limit is part of the result: an adsorbent compared at another pH would need its own fit before any ranking could be made. Within the tested scope, the framework took up the stated fraction of the dye and the fitted capacity stands as the single capacity figure the tests support for this adsorbent and this dye.
